sanskrit: rāmaḥ prekṣya tu taṃ gṛdhraṃ bhuvi raudreṇa pātitam saumitriṃ mitrasaṃpannam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing that vulture struck down to the ground by the terrible demon, Rāma spoke these words to Saumitri, who was possessed of every friendly virtue.

sanskrit: mamāyaṃ nūnam artheṣu yatamāno vihaṃgamaḥ rākṣasena hataḥ saṃkhye prāṇāṃs tyajati dustyajān
english: "This bird was surely striving for my welfare; struck down in battle by the demon, he is now giving up his life — that life so hard to surrender."

sanskrit: ayam asya śarīre 'smin prāṇo lakṣmaṇa vidyate tathā svaravihīno 'yaṃ viklavaṃ samudīkṣate
english: "There is still life in this body of his, Lakṣmaṇa; though deprived of voice, he gazes about him with bewilderment."

sanskrit: jaṭāyo yadi śaknoṣi vākyaṃ vyāharituṃ punaḥ sītām ākhyāhi bhadraṃ te vadham ākhyāhi cātmanaḥ
english: "Jaṭāyu, if you are able to speak once more, tell me of Sītā — may it go well with you — and tell me also of your own wounding."

sanskrit: kiṃnimitto 'harat sītāṃ rāvaṇas tasya kiṃ mayā aparāddhaṃ tu yaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇena hṛtā priyā
english: "For what reason did Rāvaṇa carry off Sītā? What wrong had I done him, seeing which Rāvaṇa abducted my beloved?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ tac candrasaṃkāśaṃ mukham āsīn manoharam sītayā kāni coktāni tasmin kāle dvijottama
english: "How was that moon-like, heart-ravishing face of hers? And what words did Sītā speak at that time, O foremost of birds?"

sanskrit: kathaṃvīryaḥ kathaṃrūpaḥ kiṃkarmā sa ca rākṣasaḥ kva cāsya bhavanaṃ tāta brūhi me paripṛcchataḥ
english: "What is the might, what the form, and what the deeds of that demon? And where is his dwelling? Tell me, dear one, as I ask you these things."

sanskrit: tam udvīkṣyātha dīnātmā vilapantam anantaram vācātisannayā rāmaṃ jaṭāyur idam abravīt
english: Looking up at him lamenting thus, Jaṭāyu then spoke these words to Rāma in a voice that had grown extremely faint.

sanskrit: sā hṛtā rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena vihāyasā māyām āsthāya vipulāṃ vātadurdinasaṃkulām
english: "She was carried off through the sky by Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, who had assumed a great illusion filled with wind and storm-cloud."

sanskrit: pariśrāntasya me tāta pakṣau chittvā niśācaraḥ sītām ādāya vaidehīṃ prayāto dakṣiṇā mukhaḥ
english: "Having cut off my wings, dear one, while I was utterly exhausted, that night-roamer took Vaidehī Sītā and departed facing southward."

sanskrit: uparudhyanti me prāṇā dṛṣṭir bhramati rāghava paśyāmi vṛkṣān sauvarṇān uśīrakṛtamūrdhajān
english: "My life is being arrested, my sight grows dim, O Rāghava; I see golden trees with shoots of uśīra grass for their crests."

sanskrit: yena yāti muhūrtena sītām ādāya rāvaṇaḥ vipranaṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ kṣipraṃ tat svāmipratipadyate
english: "In that same auspicious moment in which Rāvaṇa departed carrying Sītā, lost wealth swiftly returns to its owner."

sanskrit: vindo nāma muhūrto 'sau sa ca kākutstha nābudhat jhaṣavad baḍiśaṃ gṛhya kṣipram eva vinaśyati
english: "That moment is called Vinda, but he, O scion of Kākutstha, did not understand it; like a fish that seizes the hook, he will quickly perish."

sanskrit: na ca tvayā vyathā kāryā janakasya sutāṃ prati vaidehyā raṃsyase kṣipraṃ hatvā taṃ rākṣasaṃ raṇe
english: "And you should feel no anguish regarding the daughter of Janaka; you will quickly rejoice with Vaidehī after slaying that demon in battle."

sanskrit: asaṃmūḍhasya gṛdhrasya rāmaṃ pratyanubhāṣataḥ āsyāt susrāva rudhiraṃ mriyamāṇasya sāmiṣam
english: Even as that clear-minded vulture spoke these words back to Rāma, blood mixed with flesh flowed from the mouth of the dying bird.

sanskrit: putro viśravasaḥ sākṣād bhrātā vaiśravaṇasya ca ity uktvā durlabhān prāṇān mumoca patageśvaraḥ
english: "He is the direct son of Viśravas and the brother of Vaiśravaṇa" — having uttered these words, the lord of birds relinquished his life, so hard to surrender.

sanskrit: brūhi brūhīti rāmasya bruvāṇasya kṛtāñjaleḥ tyaktvā śarīraṃ gṛdhrasya jagmuḥ prāṇā vihāyasaṃ
english: As Rāma stood with palms joined, saying "Speak, speak!", the vital breaths of the vulture departed from his body into the sky.

sanskrit: sa nikṣipya śiro bhūmau prasārya caraṇau tadā vikṣipya ca śarīraṃ svaṃ papāta dharaṇītale
english: Then, lowering his head to the ground, stretching out his feet, and convulsing his own body, he fell upon the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ gṛdhraṃ prekṣya tāmrākṣaṃ gatāsum acalopamam rāmaḥ subahubhir duḥkhair dīnaḥ saumitrim abravīt
english: Beholding that red-eyed vulture, his life departed, motionless as a mountain, Rāma — overcome with many sorrows — said to Saumitri:

sanskrit: bahūni rakṣasāṃ vāse varṣāṇi vasatā sukham anena daṇḍakāraṇye vicīrṇam iha pakṣiṇā
english: "Many years were happily passed by this bird dwelling here in the Daṇḍaka forest, which is under the sway of demons."

sanskrit: anekavārṣiko yas tu cirakālaṃ samutthitaḥ so 'yam adya hataḥ śete kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: "He who had risen up and lived for so many years, for such a long time — he lies slain today; for time is indeed impossible to transgress."

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa gṛdhro 'yam upakārī hataś ca me sītām abhyavapan no vai rāvaṇena balīyasā
english: "Look, Lakṣmaṇa — this vulture who was my benefactor has been slain; he rushed to shield Sītā against the all-powerful Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: gṛdhrarājyaṃ parityajya pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat mama hetor ayaṃ prāṇān mumoca patageśvaraḥ
english: "Forsaking his great ancestral realm — the kingship of the vultures inherited from his fathers and forefathers — this lord of birds gave up his life for my sake."

sanskrit: sarvatra khalu dṛśyante sādhavo dharmacāriṇaḥ śūrāḥ śaraṇyāḥ saumitre tiryagyonigateṣv api
english: "Indeed, virtuous men — those who walk in dharma, heroes who offer refuge — are seen everywhere, Saumitri, even among those born as animals."

sanskrit: sītāharaṇajaṃ duḥkhaṃ na me saumya tathāgatam yathā vināśo gṛdhrasya matkṛte ca paraṃtapa
english: "The grief born of Sītā's abduction has not struck me so hard, O gentle one, O scorcher of foes, as the death of this vulture for my sake."

sanskrit: rājā daśarathaḥ śrīmān yathā mama mayā yaśāḥ pūjanīyaś ca mānyaś ca tathāyaṃ patageśvaraḥ
english: "Just as the illustrious King Daśaratha, so glorious, is to be worshipped and honored by me, so too is this lord of birds."

sanskrit: saumitre hara kāṣṭhāni nirmathiṣyāmi pāvakam gṛdhrarājaṃ didhakṣāmi matkṛte nidhanaṃ gatam
english: "Saumitri, bring wood; I shall kindle fire. I wish to cremate the king of vultures who has met his death for my sake."

sanskrit: nāthaṃ patagalokasya citām āropayāmy aham imaṃ dhakṣyāmi saumitre hataṃ raudreṇa rakṣasā
english: "I shall place upon the funeral pyre the lord of the bird-world and cremate him, O Saumitri — this one slain by the terrible demon."

sanskrit: yā gatir yajñaśīlānām āhitāgneś ca yā gatiḥ aparāvartināṃ yā ca yā ca bhūmipradāyinām
english: "Whatever the way gone by those devoted to sacrifice, whatever the way of those who have established the sacred fire, whatever the way of those who do not turn back in battle, and of those who give away the earth —"

sanskrit: mayā tvaṃ samanujñāto gaccha lokān anuttamān gṛdhrarāja mahāsattva saṃskṛtaś ca mayā vraja
english: "— granted permission by me, go to those highest realms, O king of vultures, O great being! Duly consecrated by me, depart."

sanskrit: evam uktvā citāṃ dīptām āropya patageśvaram dadāha rāmo dharmātmā svabandhum iva duḥkhitaḥ
english: Having spoken thus and placed the lord of birds upon the blazing pyre, the righteous-souled Rāma cremated him with grief, as though he were his own kinsman.

sanskrit: rāmo 'tha sahasaumitrir vanaṃ yātvā sa vīryavān sthūlān hatvā mahārohīn anu tastāra taṃ dvijam
english: Then valiant Rāma, together with Saumitri, went into the forest; after slaying large rohiṇī deer, he spread them out as an offering over the bird.

sanskrit: rohimāṃsāni coddhṛtya peśīkṛtvā mahāyaśāḥ śakunāya dadau rāmo ramye haritaśādvale
english: Taking out the deer-flesh and shaping it into portions, the greatly glorious Rāma offered it to the bird upon a lovely green lawn.

sanskrit: yat tat pretasya martyasya kathayanti dvijātayaḥ tat svargagamanaṃ tasya kṣipraṃ rāmo jajāpa ha
english: That which the twice-born declare concerning the passage of a mortal soul to heaven — that rite of passage — Rāma quickly recited for his sake.

sanskrit: tato godāvarīṃ gatvā nadīṃ naravarātmajau udakaṃ cakratus tasmai gṛdhrarājāya tāv ubhau
english: Then the two sons of that best of men went to the Godāvarī river and both of them offered water oblations to the king of vultures.

sanskrit: sa gṛdhrarājaḥ kṛtavān yaśaskaraṃ suduṣkaraṃ karma raṇe nipātitaḥ maharṣikalpenas ca saṃskṛtas tadā jagāma puṇyāṃ gatim ātmanaḥ śubhām
english: That king of vultures, who had performed a glorious and exceedingly difficult deed, who had been felled in battle, who was then consecrated in accordance with the rites fitting a great sage — he attained the pure and auspicious state befitting his own soul.

sanskrit: kṛtvaivam udakaṃ tasmai prasthitau rāghavau tadā avekṣantau vane sītāṃ paścimāṃ jagmatur diśam
english: Having thus offered the water oblation to him, the two Rāghavas set out, searching for Sītā in the forest, and proceeded toward the western quarter.

sanskrit: tāṃ diśaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ gatvā śaracāpāsidhāriṇau aviprahatam aikṣvākau panthānaṃ pratipedatuḥ
english: Going toward the southern quarter, bearing arrows, bows, and swords, the two sons of Ikṣvāku found an unobstructed path.

sanskrit: gulmair vṛkṣaiś ca bahubhir latābhiś ca praveṣṭitam āvṛtaṃ sarvato durgaṃ gahanaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: It was entangled with many shrubs, trees, and creepers; hemmed in on all sides, difficult of access, dense, and fearsome to behold.

sanskrit: vyatikramya tu vegena gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam subhīmaṃ tan mahāraṇyaṃ vyatiyātau mahābalau
english: Swiftly passing through, taking the southern direction, the two mighty heroes traversed that vast and formidable great forest.

sanskrit: tataḥ paraṃ janasthānāt trikrośaṃ gamya rāghavau krauñcāraṇyaṃ viviśatur gahanaṃ tau mahaujasau
english: Then, proceeding three krośas beyond Janasthāna, the two Rāghavas of great splendor entered the dense Krauñca forest.

sanskrit: nānāmeghaghanaprakhyaṃ prahṛṣṭam iva sarvataḥ nānāvarṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ puṣpair mṛgapakṣigaṇair yutam
english: It resembled a mass of various storm-clouds; it appeared joyful on all sides, adorned with flowers of many beautiful colors, and filled with herds of deer and flocks of birds.

sanskrit: didṛkṣamāṇau vaidehīṃ tad vanaṃ tau vicikyatuḥ tatra tatrāvatiṣṭhantau sītāharaṇakarśitau
english: Desiring to see Vaidehī, the two searched through that forest, pausing here and there, worn thin by the abduction of Sītā.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas tu mahātejāḥ sattvavāñ śīlavāñ śuciḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ bhrātaraṃ dīptatejasaṃ
english: Then the greatly resplendent Lakṣmaṇa — possessed of courage, good conduct, and purity — spoke with joined palms to his brother of blazing splendor:

sanskrit: spandate me dṛḍhaṃ bāhur udvignam iva me manaḥ prāyaśaś cāpy aniṣṭāni nimittāny upalakṣaye
english: "My arm throbs strongly; my mind seems agitated; and for the most part I perceive ill omens all around."

sanskrit: tasmāt sajjībhavārya tvaṃ kuruṣva vacanaṃ hitam mamaiva hi nimittāni sadyaḥ śaṃsanti saṃbhramam
english: "Therefore, noble one, be ready and heed my beneficial counsel, for the omens on my own body proclaim imminent confusion."

sanskrit: eṣa vañculako nāma pakṣī paramadāruṇaḥ āvayor vijayaṃ yuddhe śaṃsann iva vinardati
english: "This bird called the vañculaka, most dreadful, cries out as if proclaiming victory for us in battle."

sanskrit: tayor anveṣator evaṃ sarvaṃ tad vanam ojasā saṃjajñe vipulaḥ śabdaḥ prabhañjann iva tad vanam
english: While the two of them searched thus throughout that forest with their combined might, a tremendous sound arose, as if it would shatter that very forest.

sanskrit: saṃveṣṭitam ivātyarthaṃ gahanaṃ mātariśvanā vanasya tasya śabdo 'bhūd divam āpūrayann iva
english: The sound of that dense forest, as if excessively tossed about by the wind, arose filling heaven itself.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇas tu rāmaḥ kakṣe sahānujaḥ dadarśa sumahākāyaṃ rākṣasaṃ vipulorasaṃ
english: Hearkening to that sound with his brother in the brushwood, Rāma saw a demon of immense body and broad chest.

sanskrit: āsedatus tatas tatra tāv ubhau pramukhe sthitam vivṛddham aśirogrīvaṃ kabandham udare mukham
english: Then both of them approached him as he stood before them — that monstrous Kabandha, who had neither head nor neck, with his mouth set in his belly.

sanskrit: romabhir nicitais tīkṣṇaiḥ mahāgirim ivocchritam nīlameghanibhaṃ raudraṃ meghastanitaniḥsvanam
english: He was bristling with thick, sharp hairs; tall as a great mountain; resembling a dark cloud; terrible; his voice like the thunder of storm-clouds.

sanskrit: mahāpakṣmeṇa piṅgena vipulenāyatena ca ekenorasi ghoreṇa nayanenāśudarśinā
english: He had a single eye on his chest — tawny, with great lashes, wide and elongated, terrible, keen-sighted.

sanskrit: mahādaṃṣṭropapannaṃ taṃ lelihānaṃ mahāmukham bhakṣayantaṃ mahāghorān ṛkṣasiṃhamṛgadvipān
english: Furnished with great fangs, licking his enormous mouth, he was devouring the most dreadful bears, lions, deer, and elephants.

sanskrit: ghorau bhujau vikurvāṇam ubhau yojanam āyatau karābhyāṃ vividhān gṛhya ṛṣkān pakṣigaṇān mṛgān
english: Extending his two terrible arms, each a yojana in length, he was seizing with his hands various bears, flocks of birds, and animals.

sanskrit: ākarṣantaṃ vikarṣantam anekān mṛgayūthapān sthitam āvṛtya panthānaṃ tayor bhrātroḥ prapannayoḥ
english: Drawing in and dragging out many leaders of animal herds, he stood blocking the path of those two brothers who had fallen into his reach.

sanskrit: atha tau samatikramya krośamātre dadarśatuḥ mahāntaṃ dāruṇaṃ bhīmaṃ kabandhaṃ bhujasaṃvṛtam
english: Then, as the two pressed forward, at the distance of a krośa they saw the great, dreadful, and fearsome Kabandha, enveloped by his own arms.

sanskrit: sa mahābāhur atyarthaṃ prasārya vipulau bhujau jagrāha sahitāv eva rāghavau pīḍayan balāt
english: He of the great arms extended his two vast arms to the utmost and seized both Rāghavas together, squeezing them forcibly.

sanskrit: khaḍginau dṛḍhadhanvānau tigmatejau mahābhujau bhrātarau vivaśaṃ prāptau kṛṣyamāṇau mahābalau
english: Those two brothers — bearing swords, clutching their firm bows, blazing with fierce energy, great-armed — fell helpless into his power and were being dragged along by the mighty one.

sanskrit: tāv uvāca mahābāhuḥ kabandho dānavottamaḥ kau yuvāṃ vṛṣabhaskandhau mahākhaḍgadhanurdharau
english: Kabandha, the foremost of dānavas, great-armed, spoke to the two: "Who are you, bull-shouldered ones, bearing great swords and bows?"

sanskrit: ghoraṃ deśam imaṃ prāptau mama bhakṣāv upasthitau vadataṃ kāryam iha vāṃ kimarthaṃ cāgatau yuvām
english: "Having reached this dreadful region, you have come as food for me. Speak of your business here — for what purpose have the two of you come?"

sanskrit: imaṃ deśam anuprāptau kṣudhārtasyeha tiṣṭhataḥ sabāṇacāpakhaḍgau ca tīkṣṇaśṛṅgāv ivarṣabhau mamāsyam anusaṃprāptau durlabhaṃ jīvitaṃ punaḥ
english: "Having arrived in this region where I stand tormented by hunger, bearing arrows, bows, and swords, like two bulls with sharp horns, you have approached my mouth; life will be hard to regain."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kabandhasya durātmanaḥ uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ rāmo mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: Having heard those words of evil-souled Kabandha, Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa with face grown parched:

sanskrit: kṛcchrāt kṛcchrataraṃ prāpya dāruṇaṃ satyavikrama vyasanaṃ jīvitāntāya prāptam aprāpya tāṃ priyām
english: "Having encountered calamity upon calamity, O truly valiant one, we have arrived at this dreadful misfortune that brings life to an end — and still without finding my beloved."

sanskrit: kālasya sumahad vīryaṃ sarvabhūteṣu lakṣmaṇa tvāṃ ca māṃ ca naravyāghra vyasanaiḥ paśya mohitau nātibhāro 'sti daivasya sarvabhuteṣu lakṣmaṇa
english: "The power of Time is exceedingly great over all beings, Lakṣmaṇa; behold both you and me, O tiger among men, bewildered by misfortune. The burden of fate is not too heavy upon all creatures, Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: śūrāś ca balavantaś ca kṛtāstrāś ca raṇājire kālābhipannāḥ sīdanti yathā vālukasetavaḥ
english: "Heroes, the mighty, those skilled in arms on the battlefield — when overtaken by Time they sink down like embankments of sand."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇo dṛḍhasatyavikramo mahāyaśā dāśarathiḥ pratāpavān avekṣya saumitrim udagravikramaṃ sthirāṃ tadā svāṃ matim ātmanākarot
english: Speaking thus, the son of Daśaratha — of firm and true valor, greatly glorious, of high majesty — looking upon Saumitri of lofty valor, then made his own resolve steadfast within himself.

sanskrit: tau tu tatra sthitau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau bāhupāśaparikṣiptau kabandho vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing those two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa standing there, ensnared in the coils of his arms, Kabandha spoke:

sanskrit: tiṣṭhataḥ kiṃ nu māṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣudhārtaṃ kṣatriyarṣabhau āhārārthaṃ tu saṃdiṣṭau daivena gatacetasau
english: "Why do you two stand here looking at me, O bulls among kṣatriyas, tormented by hunger? Surely fate has ordained you as my food, your minds now lost."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā lakṣmaṇo vākyaṃ prāptakālaṃ hitaṃ tadā uvācārtisamāpanno vikrame kṛtaniścayaḥ
english: Having heard those words, Lakṣmaṇa — overwhelmed with pain yet resolved upon a course of action — then spoke words that were timely and beneficial:

sanskrit: tvāṃ ca māṃ ca purā tūrṇam ādatte rākṣasādhamaḥ tasmād asibhyām asyāśu bāhū chindāvahe gurū
english: "This lowest of demons is quickly swallowing both you and me; therefore let us swiftly cut off his two great arms with our swords."

sanskrit: tatas tau deśakālajñau khaḍgābhyām eva rāghavau acchindatāṃ susaṃhṛṣṭau bāhū tasyāṃsadeśayoḥ
english: Then those two Rāghavas, knowing time and place, with their swords and with great exhilaration severed both his arms at the shoulder joints.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇo dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum asaktam asinā tataḥ ciccheda rāmo vegena savyaṃ vīras tu lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Rāma on the right cut the right arm cleanly with his sword in one swift stroke, while heroic Lakṣmaṇa cut the left.

sanskrit: sa papāta mahābāhuś chinnabāhur mahāsvanaḥ khaṃ ca gāṃ ca diśaś caiva nādayañ jalado yathā
english: He of the great arms fell, his arms severed, making a tremendous sound, filling the sky, the earth, and all the quarters, like a storm cloud.

sanskrit: sa nikṛttau bhujau dṛṣṭvā śoṇitaughapariplutaḥ dīnaḥ papraccha tau vīrau kau yuvām iti dānavaḥ
english: Seeing his arms cut off, drenched in a flood of blood, that dānava pitiably asked those two heroes: "Who are you?"

sanskrit: iti tasya bruvāṇasya lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ śaśaṃsa tasya kākutsthaṃ kabandhasya mahābalaḥ
english: As he spoke thus, the auspiciously marked and mighty Lakṣmaṇa proclaimed Kākutstha to Kabandha.

sanskrit: ayam ikṣvākudāyādo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ asyaivāvarajaṃ viddhi bhrātaraṃ māṃ ca lakṣmaṇam
english: "This is the heir of the Ikṣvāku lineage, known among men by the name Rāma; and know me, Lakṣmaṇa, as his younger brother."

sanskrit: asya devaprabhāvasya vasato vijane vane rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā yām icchantāv ihāgatau
english: "This one of divine might has been dwelling in the desolate forest; his wife has been carried off by a demon, and it is in search of her that the two of us have come here."

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu ko vā kimarthaṃ vā kabandha sadṛśo vane āsyenorasi dīptena bhagnajaṅgho viceṣṭase
english: "But who are you, and for what reason do you writhe in the forest in this form resembling a Kabandha, with a blazing mouth in your chest and your legs broken?"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ kabandhas tu lakṣmaṇenottaraṃ vacaḥ uvāca paramaprītas tad indravacanaṃ smaran
english: Thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa, Kabandha spoke his reply, supremely delighted, recalling the words of Indra.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ vāṃ naravyāghrau diṣṭyā paśyāmi cāpy aham diṣṭyā cemau nikṛttau me yuvābhyāṃ bāhubandhanau
english: "Welcome, O tigers among men! By good fortune I behold you, and by good fortune these arms of mine that have been my bondage have now been severed by the two of you."

sanskrit: virūpaṃ yac ca me rūpaṃ prāptaṃ hy avinayād yathā tan me śṛṇu naravyāghra tattvataḥ śaṃsatas tava
english: "And this disfigured form of mine — how it was obtained through insolence — hear that from me, O tiger among men, as I tell you the truth of it."
